misreadings.quote: even 'a tender memory' of a cashier
misreadings.evidence: one of the chambermaids from a provincial hotel, a tender memory that appeared and disappeared again, a cashier from a hat shop for whom his attention had been serious but too slow
misreadings.explanation: The text calls the chambermaid the 'tender memory'; the cashier is a separate figure described as someone his attention was 'serious but too slow' for.

misreadings.quote: he realizes that his professional memories—the salesmen, the apprentices, even 'a tender memory' of a cashier—are fading.
misreadings.evidence: he had long forgotten about his boss and the chief clerk, but they would appear again in his thoughts, the salesmen and the apprentices... all of them appeared to him... and he was glad when they disappeared.
misreadings.explanation: The text says the long-forgotten figures reappear in his thoughts and then vanish again; it does not say Gregor realizes his memories are fading.

misreadings.quote: He’s starting to realize that his professional memories—the salesmen, the apprentices, even a tender memory of a cashier—are fading away.
misreadings.evidence: he had long forgotten about his boss and the chief clerk, but they would appear again in his thoughts... and he was glad when they disappeared.
misreadings.explanation: The figures come back into his mind and then disappear; Gregor is not described as realizing a gradual fading of his memories.

result.note: Most of the reflection is interpretation; the only clear factual error is attributing the 'tender memory' to the cashier instead of the chambermaid, plus a mild misdescription of the memories as fading when the text has them reappearing.
